card: Reject empty overflow pages as database corruption in the read-only Berkeley DB parser. When an overflow page contains zero data and references itself as the next page, parsing loops infinitely, pinning a CPU core at 100% and blocking wallet dumping or migratewallet RPC calls from completing. Author benchmarks confirm the hang on master and immediate failure under this PR, accompanied by a test in tool_wallet.py.
evidence: Author's benchmarks show a synthetic 5-page BDB file with a self-referencing empty overflow page spins at 100% CPU until killed (60s/90s) on master, whereas with this PR bitcoin-wallet dump fails immediately with exit code 1.
Author observed that migratewallet on master hangs an HTTP RPC worker thread indefinitely and prevents node stop from finishing within 30 seconds.
problem: When parsing an overflow record, the loop stops only when next_page is zero or the accumulated data exceeds the expected record length. An empty overflow page (hf_offset of 0) adds no bytes; if it points to itself, the loop never terminates, causing commands like bitcoin-wallet dump or migratewallet to spin at 100% CPU on a worker thread and preventing clean node shutdown.

risk.why: A false positive check in the BDB reader could reject valid legacy wallet files during wallet dumping or migration.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the input, but the PR consists of a validation check in BerkeleyRODatabase and a test in tool_wallet.py.
summary: Reject empty overflow pages as corruption when parsing read-only Berkeley DB files in BerkeleyRODatabase::Open. This prevents an infinite loop when a corrupted or maliciously crafted BDB overflow page with zero data links back to itself.
